# Chrome <img> sizing (M6-T0 probe)
# Source: tmp/m6probe/img.py + common.js + run.js, 2026-11-26 (dev-only probe, never Go code). kind dom: chromium --headless --dump-dom, getBoundingClientRect (as tmp/m3probe/run.sh); kind pdf: chromium --print-to-pdf (page 400x300 CSS px, margin 0), image positions read with pdftocairo -svg.
# Browser: Chromium 156.0.8078.108 built on Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie). Units: CSS px.
# Image $A: PNG 100x50 px (ratio 2:1, solid colour) as a data: URL, decoded before measuring (an undecoded image measures 0x0). Fonts: 'DejaVu Sans' 16px/20px.
# Format: kind dom: {"kind","name","w" (container width),"css","html" ($A = the image),"m": {key: [x,y,w,h] border box relative to the case container (display:flow-root, margin 0), 3 decimals}}.
# kind pdf: {"kind","name","html","page_css","pages","per_page":[{"page","images_bbox_px":[[x,y,w,h]...] drawn image rectangles from the page top-left}]}.
# Rules read from the data: replaced size = attributes as hints (a % attribute resolves like CSS %), CSS wins over the attribute of the same side and the other side's attribute still applies (04 i2: CSS width 200 + height=10 gives 200x10), the missing side follows the ratio of the intrinsic size,
# max-width clamps the width and the auto height follows (an explicit height attribute stays: ratio distorted), min-height/min-width/max-height on an auto-sized image keep the ratio,
# an explicit width and an explicit max-height distort; a flex item stretched in a 100px row is 200x100 (ratio kept, width follows) and does not shrink below its intrinsic width in a 50px container. Inline images sit on the baseline (bottom edge on the baseline).
